The fix is mostly sound, but it can silently alter version data, so I'm requesting changes. The incident was the site changing the Status text from "Rev. N" to "Version N.0". The fix changes one regex, and the gates passed on all 11 listed pages. Nothing else in the diff is a concern: dates are still strictly MM/DD/YYYY, the new version regex is still anchored, a non-matching Status still throws, and pagination and clause parsing are untouched.

The problem is in the new regex, `/^Version (\d+)\.\d+$/`:
- It accepts any minor number and then drops it, using only `status[1]`. A page showing "Version 2.1" would be stored as version 2, the same as "Version 2.0".
- That would mislabel a revision, or make two different revisions look identical. For compliance data it should throw instead.
- All four sample pages I checked show ".0", so this hasn't happened yet. I did not check the other pages the gates read, only the sample file.
- The safer pattern is `/^Version (\d+)\.0$/`, which fails loudly on any non-zero minor. Alternatively, the minor could be carried into the stored version if the schema allows it.

Minor point: the error message changed from "no revision" to "no version", which is harmless.
